mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate indicates monetary easing, which may stimulate economic activity and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS declines but SPX 20-day returns are not positive in most cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in unemployment rate suggests economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE rises but SPX returns remain positive.

mechanism_narrative: Rising GDP and CPI suggest inflationary pressures, which could lead to positive S&P 500 returns as companies may increase prices.
failure_condition: If both GDPC1 and CPIAUCSL rise but SPX 60-day returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: Increased industrial production indicates economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO grows but SPX 60-day returns are not positive.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in payroll employment suggests a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS grows but SPX 5-day returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: Increased retail sales indicate strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS exceeds threshold but SPX returns are not positive.

mechanism_narrative: When federal funds rate is above 4.5% and unemployment rises, it may signal economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If both conditions are met but SPX returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in housing starts indicates economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If HOUST grows but SPX 60-day returns are not positive.
